rationale: Targeted check of 3 prior blocking findings: CR-001 and CR-002 are resolved in current source (isReadOnly now drives the catalogue display; buildServerConfig takes isCatalogRef and forces use_custom_config false/config undefined, with tests). CR-003 is superseded because the string-details branch was removed entirely from processBackendError, but that fix-up also reverted the parsedError.message extraction in createAssistant/updateAssistant, which Stage 7 or a final re-review should confirm against the 'show the backend-reported reason' criterion; confidence is medium for that reason.

standards_review.notes: All 5 commit subjects in range match EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence format with real ticket id, capitalized first word, no trailing period.
No code-quality guide found at .ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md and no ArtifactRef passed for code_quality; absent standard, not a gap.

security-patterns.md checklist checked against changed files: no unsafe sinks, redirects, postMessage, env/secret reads, or nosonar additions; the isCatalogRef/isMCPRestrictedMode logic is UI-affordance only, no concrete security defect found.

findings.title: Read-only field can show stale config, not catalog
findings.problem: The read-only textarea's displayed value only checked `!useCustomConfig`, not `isCatalogRef`, so a stale custom JSON could display under a 'Global' label.
findings.impact: Misleading display of the configuration that would actually be used under governance.
findings.recommendation: Include isCatalogRef in the display condition.

findings.title: Custom config not cleared for catalogue-restricted servers
findings.problem: buildServerConfig() never received isCatalogRef and resubmitted use_custom_config true plus the old custom JSON on every save.
findings.impact: Frontend did not enforce catalogue-only config at the data layer.
findings.recommendation: Pass isCatalogRef into buildServerConfig and force use_custom_config false / config undefined.

findings.title: Empty details string leaves dangling colon
findings.problem: processBackendError appended `: ${error.details}` for any string details, including empty.
findings.impact: Dangling colon in the general error text.
findings.recommendation: Guard the branch with a non-empty check.

finding_status.notes: MCPConfigSection.tsx:138 now uses isReadOnly (= hasCatalogReference && (isCatalogRef || !useCustomConfig)) for the catalogue display; test added.
formHelpers.ts takes isCatalogRef and forces use_custom_config false and config undefined when a config id exists; MCPToolkitForm/index.tsx:86 passes isCatalogRef; tests added.

The string-details branch no longer exists in backendErrorHandler.ts (details is object-only), so the dangling-colon case is moot. Side effect: the parsedError.message extraction in the assistants store was also reverted.
